To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the List Edge Coloring conjecture holds for graphs of maximum degree 3 embedded in any surface of nonnegative characteristic; (2) the List Edge Conjecture holds for graphs with maximum degree 4 embedded in the projective plane, torus or the Klein bottle;

for any surface of nonnegative genus, there exists a threshold on the maximum degree, below which a graph is edge choosable, and that the same threshold applies to all graphs that are 1-cell embedded in the surface.
the sizes of 2-cell embedded graphs containing no cycles of specified sizes are bounded by functions of the sizes of their faces.
In summary, our research is concerned with
two main topics.

the following problem: given a graph \(G\) and a list assignment \(L\) to \(G\), is it possible to assign a color to each edge of \(G\) so that the colors of the edges incident to each vertex of \(G\) form a list assigned to that vertex and no two adjacent edges have the same color?
the size of the smallest graph that is embedded in a fixed surface and contains no cycles of specified length, and how such a bound affects the edge choosability of the graph.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Theorem A is a very nice and important result, and Theorem B is a nice and important application of Theorem A.
the list edge coloring conjecture is true for graphs of maximum degree at least 5 and 2-cell embeddable in a surface of genus 1, 2, 3, 4, or 6.

Theorem B confirms the List Edge Coloring conjecture for any graphs with maximum degree 3 and for any graphs that can be embedded in surfaces of nonnegatice Euler characteristic and have maximum degree greater than 3.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we prove that the list edge coloring conjecture holds for all 2-cell embedded graphs in surfaces of nonnegaitve Euler characteristic with maximum degree at least 7.
we have obtained a complete answer to the List Edge Coloring Problem for graphs with maximum degree at least 5 that are embeddable in a surface of Euler characteristic at most 2.
we have established some upper bounds on the size of a graph that can be embedded in a surface, and these bounds are used to show that some graphs are edge choosable.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the size of the largest cycle in a graph plays an important role in its edge choosability.
, in the context of the List Edge Coloring problem, the surface of a given genus is a much more natural setting than the sphere.
the bounds we obtain on the sizes of the graphs are much smaller than the bounds given in the previous literature.
